t.4.56.1: Though they heard his words, spoken in a voice broken by grief, those leaders of the monkey troops did not believe them at all, for they were suspicious of him because of his deed.
t.4.56.2: But those monkeys, seated in their fast unto death, saw the vulture and then formed a dreadful thought: "He will devour us all."
t.4.56.3: In any case, if he devours us as we sit fasting unto death, we shall have accomplished our purpose, having swiftly attained perfection from here.
t.4.56.4: Then all those bulls among the monkeys came to this resolve, and Aṅgada, having brought the vulture down from the mountain peak, spoke to him.
t.4.56.5: O bird, there was a mighty lord of the monkeys named Ṛkṣarajas, my noble king, and he had two righteous sons.
t.4.56.7: The king of the whole world, the great chariot-warrior of the Ikṣvākus, the glorious Rāma, son of Daśaratha, entered the Daṇḍaka forest.
t.4.56.6: Sugrīva and Vālī were both sons endowed with overwhelming strength. The king Vālī, whose deeds were renowned in the world, was my father.
t.4.56.8: Together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and his wife Vaidehī, devoted to his father's command, he took to the righteous path. His wife was carried off by force from Janasthāna by Rāvaṇa.
t.4.56.9: Jaṭāyu by name, king of the vultures and friend of Rāma's father, saw Sītā, the princess of Videha, being carried off through the sky.
t.4.56.10: Having made Rāvaṇa chariotless and having held back Maithilī, he, exhausted and old, was slain in battle by Rāvaṇa.
t.4.56.11: Thus the vulture was slain by that mighty Rāvaṇa, and he was given his funeral rites by Rāma and went to the highest state.
t.4.56.12: Then Rāghava made friendship with my paternal uncle, the great-souled Sugrīva; he slew my father.
t.4.56.14: By him was Sugrīva, lord of the vānaras, established in the kingdom, Sugrīva, king of the chief vānaras, by whom we have been sent forth.
t.4.56.13: For Sugrīva, together with his ministers, was at odds with my father; Rāma slew Vālin and then had Sugrīva consecrated as king.
t.4.56.15: Thus, though sent forth by Rāma and searching here and there, we do not find Vaidehī, just as one does not find the sun's light at night.
t.4.56.16: Having searched the Daṇḍaka forest with great attentiveness, we then, unknowingly, entered an open cavern in the earth.
t.4.56.17: And while we were searching that cave fashioned by the magic of Maya, the month that the king had fixed as our time limit passed away for us there.
t.4.56.18: We, all of us doers of the bidding of the king of monkeys, having overstepped the appointed time-limit, now out of fear resort to fasting unto death.
t.4.56.19: But when that Kākutstha is enraged, and Sugrīva too along with Lakṣmaṇa, there is no life left for any of us, even if we all go there.
